incident-bot: High severity alert: 30% throughput drop in region-us-east on Dedicated pool 'd-gpu-v2' affecting inference-slices. Triggered at 2026-02-24T10:12:01Z

alex (eng-runtime): rolling out prefetch-scheduler-v3 to dedicated today, started at 10:10. seeing spike in request queues and KV eviction. tagging @devin for oncall.

devin (oncall): I'm on it. can you paste the rollout id?

alex (eng-runtime): deploy-bot: rollout_id=rl-20260224-17. logs: 

```
# tail -n 80 /var/log/runtime/prefetch-scheduler.log
[10:12:05] INFO prefetch-scheduler: batch_coalesce: new_policy=aggressive
[10:12:07] WARN rpc: dropped 0.4% reqs due to batch_timeout
[10:12:12] ERROR kernel-manager: compat-kernel fallback triggered on node gpu-12
[10:12:14] WARN kv-cache: eviction_rate up 8x
```

maria (eng-ml): init tests looked fine in staging but we didn't mirror the slice distribution. v3 merges tiny requests into large batches which is bad for short-sequence latency. might be increasing tail and causing backpressure in the scheduler.

emily (sre): metrics: p50 ~ unchanged, p95 up 120ms, p99 up 480ms, overall tokens/sec down ~30%. hitting pod autoscaler limits, small OOM churn reported on some nodes.

deploy-bot: rollout rl-20260224-17: 40% traffic to v3 (slice policy=aggressive). Canary passed initial healthchecks.

devin (oncall): is this isolated to a subset of slices or across all models?

alex (eng-runtime): looks worse for short-seq chat models and embeddings jobs that have many small requests. long-seq models maintain throughput.

cs-alerts: customer-notify: 12 customers with elevated latency, 3 reporting timeouts. queued a banner draft for status.redwood.ai.

devin (oncall): immediate mitigation options?

alex (eng-runtime): options: 1) flip feature flag prefetch_v3_enabled=false (fast) 2) pause rollout (deployctl cancel-traffic rl-20260224-17) 3) rollback RL -> previous scheduler v2 (slower but safer). recommending kill-flag first then rollback if not fixed.

emily (sre): recommend killing flag on all Dedicated nodes in us-east to stop batch policy change propagation. I'll prepare the KMS call and runbook.

maria (eng-ml): also consider increasing KV cache capacity temporarily to reduce evictions; that's a lower-impact tweak while we flip the flag.

alex (eng-runtime): command to flip flag for Dedicated: 
```
redwoodctl flags set prefetch_v3_enabled=false --scope=d-gpu-v2 --env=prod
```

devin (oncall): running now. 

(devin runs command)

deploy-bot: flag-change: prefetch_v3_enabled=false applied to scope=d-gpu-v2 by devin at 10:20:18Z

emily (sre): seeing rollout of flag; starting to observe queue drain in metrics. p95 dropping towards baseline.

cs-alerts: updated status page: "We are investigating increased latency for some inference requests in us-east; mitigation in progress."

alex (eng-runtime): even with flag off some nodes already fell back to compat-kernel and are hot with thrash. will trigger a targeted restart of affected instances: gpu-12, gpu-14, gpu-19.

emily (sre): initiating controlled restarts on the three nodes to recover kernel state. using graceful drain: 
```
redwoodctl node restart gpu-12 --graceful
redwoodctl node restart gpu-14 --graceful
redwoodctl node restart gpu-19 --graceful
```

(deploy-bot): node restart scheduled. expected 60s drain per node.

maria (eng-ml): after restarts, please re-run synthetic short-seq load against embeddings endpoint to confirm tail latency.

(devin monitors metrics)

deploy-bot: node gpu-12 back online at 10:24:51Z; gpu-14 back online at 10:25:38Z; gpu-19 back online at 10:26:29Z

emily (sre): metrics: tokens/sec recovering to ~92% baseline, p95 close to baseline, p99 improving but still slightly elevated (~+80ms). no new OOMs.

alex (eng-runtime): good. I'll schedule a rollback of rl-20260224-17 for the remainder of the pool to be safe. plan: revert rollout to scheduler v2 config and run longer running soak in canary for 2 hours.

devin (oncall): execute rollback when ready. Coordinate with deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: starting rollback of rl-20260224-17 -> rl-20260224-16 (target config: prefetch-scheduler-v2) at 10:31:02Z

cs-alerts: updated customers: mitigation applied, performance improving. advising customers to retry. logged 3 support tickets escalated for high priority.

maria (eng-ml): postmortem notes: regression triggered by aggressive coalescing heuristics that weren't exercised by staging request distribution. add a synthetic short-seq harness in CI and a staging config that mirrors production slice sizes.

emily (sre): handoff plan: I'll keep monitoring for the next 2 hours, then hand over to oncall-night if stable. We'll also queue an incident page for follow-up actions: root-cause, QA changes, and rollout process improvement.

devin (oncall): documenting timeline and actions in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incident/1767504321 (draft).

alex (eng-runtime): follow-ups I'll own: 1) make prefetch policy opt-in for Dedicated pools 2) add KV cache observability for eviction rates per-slice 3) post-rollback canary with better slice matching.

cs-alerts: created support ticket bundle and pinged the 12 customers with explanation and ETA. no legal or billing escalations so far.

emily (sre): current status: mitigated (flag flip + targeted restarts + rollback in progress). impact reduced, monitoring for regression. handoff to @devin in 1h unless new alerts. :white_check_mark:

devin (oncall): acknowledged. taking primary ownership for next hour, then handoff to night oncall. tagging @maria for follow-up CI changes.

alex (eng-runtime): thanks all. I'll follow up in the incident doc with repro and tests.

incident-bot: Incident 1767504321 status: MITIGATED -> monitoring. severity->sev2.

(devin adds final note)

deployment timeline: 10:10 roll started -> 10:12 metrics alerted -> 10:20 feature flag off -> 10:24 node restarts -> 10:31 rollback started -> 10:40 metrics near baseline.

end of thread
